        "All 530 owned diff lines across 12 paths were read, including each changed test cleanup. Converted removals await removeLoginAsync in Calendar, Chat, LDAP, OAuth and SMTP internals.         "Public synchronous prompt, account-removal and server-forget interfaces remain synchronous. New wrappers use a finished flag, Promise callbacks and spinEventLoopUntilOrQuit. MsgAuthPrompt result starts false, changes only on fulfillment and returns after settlement; rejection is not rethrown through the public call and the resulting rejected chain has no catch. Its actual incoming-server caller maps false to NS_ERROR_ABORT. Calendar asyncPromptAuth likewise starts its internal Promise without returning it, while its usable-credential path deliberately dispatches the callback after the public call returns.",
        "FinalizeSignonDeletions suppresses storage-triggered display reload, awaits removals one by one, then restores reloadDisplay and clears deletedSignons. A rejected removal skips those later statements; no finally restores the flag. The actual observer checks this flag before reload, and DeleteAllSignons updates the tree before awaiting finalization. This is a static failure-path limit, not an observed UI failure.",
        "The converted Calendar lookup retains a pre-existing branch returning { found: false, username } after rejecting a recently returned password. Both the original new synchronous wrapper and the async branch test that value by truthiness, despite the Boolean return documentation. The accepted later request-scoped PREVIOUS_FAILED branch returns false instead. This is a retained original contract mismatch and later difference, not a claim that this migration introduced the object branch or that the later fix was exercised.",
        "OAuth clearTokens clears memory before awaiting persisted deletion. SMTP clears its password cache before awaited deletion and awaits clearTokens; incoming-server forgetting clears its cache later. LDAP awaits deletion before retrying its prompt, but the inspected message dispatcher does not consume the Promise. Original Chat removal waits for password deletion before account teardown; accepted Chat instead explicitly removes the password without waiting after teardown. These receiver-specific differences prevent a blanket asynchronous-completion claim.",
